topics.narration: Under the streets of Derinkuyu, a city drops about 280 feet (85 meters), according to Turkey's culture ministry. At least eight levels are commonly cited. One ventilation shaft, about 180 feet (55 meters) deep, doubled as a water well. Estimates suggest it could have sheltered thousands, perhaps up to 20,000 people. Its rolling stone doors are often said to weigh several hundred kilograms, though no official figure is known. Who dug first is uncertain: some say Hittites, others Phrygians. In the middle Byzantine period, it was greatly expanded as a refuge from raids. Only about ten percent can be visited today; the rest lies under the streets of Derinkuyu.
